title: What Two Million Canary Prompts Reveal About AI Supply Chain Security
content_md: Executive Summary To evaluate the security of the AI supply chain, Dragos seeded approximately two million AI prompts with canary URLs and credentials. The investigation revealed that prompt data was stolen from at least three AI hosting providers and from the system of a Chinese AI lab, which accessed secret URLs from prompts marked for zero data retention. No security team can audit the providers its prompts pass through, whether they are foreign or domestic. Every team can test its own side: the models it calls and what goes into each prompt. Qualys TotalAI maps the models and AI services in use, red-teams any model with a chat completion endpoint (including foreign models), and detects secrets before they reach a prompt. Inside the Canary Experiment In a study published on November 19, 2026 , a team from Dragos, led by Chief Research Officer HD Moore, sent approximately two million prompts to popular AI services from July through November, tracing around 2,000 request routes. Each prompt carried canary tokens: unique URLs and live AWS keys linked to empty accounts that were fully monitored. If a URL was accessed, it indicated that the system had read the prompt; if a key was used, it showed that someone had stolen a credential. What the Dragos Canary Study Exposed Breached Providers Attackers have stolen prompt data from at least three AI hosting providers, and Dragos reports that these providers were unaware of the breaches until they were notified.
